headline: ‘Rs 92cr assets linked to drug trafficking seized’: Sukhu at anti-chitta walkathon in Mandi
content: Shimla: Himachal Pradesh chief minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu said on Friday that the state govt had seized assets worth Rs 92 crore allegedly linked to drug trafficking and demolished 22 properties built on govt land as part of its crackdown on chitta.Leading an anti-chitta awareness walkathon in Mandi, Sukhu said the govt was following a strict policy against drug traffickers but stressed that curbing the menace required a collective effort by all sections of society.“There is no place in Himachal Pradesh for those who sell chitta and destroy the lives of our youth for money,” he said while addressing a gathering at Paddal Ground.The walkathon, which began and concluded at Paddal Ground after passing through the Bus Stand and Seri Manch, saw participation of several by students and locals. The CM also administered an anti-chitta pledge to the participants.Sukhu appealed to people to share credible information with the authorities through the emergency toll-free number 112. He said govt had also made provisions to reward those providing accurate and reliable information about drug traffickers.The chief minister said the campaign, launched nearly a year ago, was being transformed into a people’s movement. Recalling its earlier events, he said thousands had participated in an anti-drug rally in Shimla on Nov 5, 2025, followed by programmes in Dharamshala, Hamirpur, Una and Bilaspur.He said the same spirit of public participation was visible in Mandi and particularly appreciated students who had travelled from remote parts of the district to join the walkathon.Earlier, the CM laid the foundation stone of a district library building in Mandi, to be constructed at a cost of Rs 6.5 crore.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Sukhu urges youth to join fight against drugs, says assets worth Rs 92 crore seized
content: Mandi/Shimla (HP), Nov 13 (PTI) Himachal Pradesh Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu on Friday said assets worth Rs 92 crore, allegedly acquired through illegal drug activities, had been seized so far, asserting that there was no place in the state for those involved in selling chitta. Leading an anti-chitta awareness walkathon in Mandi, Sukhu appealed to people, particularly the youth, to actively participate in the fight against drug abuse and help make the state drug-free. “I want to make it absolutely clear that there is no place in Himachal Pradesh for those who sell chitta and destroy the lives of our youth for money,” he said in a statement. He said the government had adopted a firm policy against those involved in the illegal drug trade and was taking strict legal action against drug peddlers and traffickers. The walkathon started from Paddal Ground in Mandi town, proceeded towards the bus stand and Seri Manch, and returned to Paddal Ground. A large number of students and local residents from across the district participated in the event. On the occasion, the chief minister administered an anti-chitta pledge to the participants and urged them to remain alert and contribute actively to the campaign against drug abuse.

headline: Union Minister Nitin Gadkari Unveils ₹3 Lakh Crore Road Infrastructure Roadmap for Andhra Pradesh at 31st CII Summit in Visakhapatnam
content: Union Minister for Road Transport and Highways, Shri Nitin Gadkari, today addressed the 31st Confederation of Indian Industry (CII) Summit in Visakhapatnam, outlining a transformative road infrastructure programme for Andhra Pradesh aligned with the vision of Viksit Bharat under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. Speaking on the theme of “Roads as the Foundation of Economic Growth”, he stressed that quality road infrastructure is essential for reducing logistics costs, attracting investment, generating jobs and driving prosperity. Shri Gadkari informed that projects worth approximately ₹3 lakh crore are under implementation or planned in the state. Of these, projects costing ₹60,000 crore covering 4,750 km have already been completed; projects worth ₹1 lakh crore covering 2,500 km are ongoing; and upgrading works of ₹1.20 lakh crore covering 4,600 km are in progress. The national highway network in Andhra Pradesh has nearly doubled—from 4,100 km in 2014 to 8,700 km in 2026. These are being implemented in close consultation with the Government of Andhra Pradesh and are in line with the vision of Chief Minister Shri N. Chandrababu Naidu. Given Andhra Pradesh’s long coastline and major ports, the Minister emphasised the strategic importance of port-led development (building on the earlier Sagarmala initiative). Key initiatives include the Kharagpur–Visakhapatnam–Amaravati corridor (1,100 km, ₹71,000 crore overall; Andhra Pradesh portion 460 km, ₹30,000 crore), with Detailed Project Report under preparation, providing direct connectivity to Visakhapatnam, Gangavaram, Kakinada and Machilipatnam ports. Multiple dedicated port connectivity roads for Visakhapatnam, Kakinada and Krishnapatnam ports are under construction or in advanced stages. The Minister informed that, the proposed Amaravati Outer Ring Road (190 km, ₹32,000 crore) has received Public-Private Partnership Appraisal Committee appraisal and awaits Cabinet approval. It will cover parts of NTR, Krishna, Guntur and Palnadu districts, decongest urban centres, and support industrial parks and logistics hubs. Several bypasses (including Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and others) are also under implementation.

headline: Ethanol Blending: Karnataka Questions Centre’s E20 Policy and Oversight
content: ah84UJE9 E20 Petrol Controversy: Karnataka Minister Rizwan Arshad Challenges Centre Ethanol content of up to 31.2 per cent was found in petrol samples collected across Karnataka, exceeding the prescribed 20 per cent limit, according to a Karnataka State government investigation. Karnataka’s Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister Rizwan Arshad, who spearheaded the investigation, has accused oil marketing companies of failing to ensure transparency in the quality and quantity of petrol dispensed to consumers. Frontline 1788 16:9 E20 controversey The Karnataka government’s recent investigation into the ethanol content of fuel dispensed at various petrol outlets in the State, and subsequent claim that it exceeded the 20 per cent limit in several instances, has sparked off a major controversy. While the oil companies rejected this claim and criticised the methodology, the Karnataka government has stood its ground. This has come just months after a massive uproar against the very use of E20 petrol (a blended fuel consisting of 20 per cent ethanol and 80 per cent standard petrol), which could reduce mileage and damage vehicles, usually older models, that are not compatible with it. https://frontline.thehindu.com/news/ethanol-blending-e20-petrol-karnataka-oil-companies-controversy/article71689181.ece https://frontline.thehindu.com/the-nation/agriculture/india-ethanol-policy-e20-costs/article71383485.ece Speaking to Frontline, Karnataka’s Food, Civil Supplies and Consumer Affairs Minister Rizwan Arshad, who spearheaded the drive, elaborated on the investigation, his criticism of the oil companies and the Narendra Modi-led Central government, and the State government’s next move. Excerpts: Of late, you have seriously taken up issues concerning the quality and quantity of the petrol dispensed to the public. What prompted the current investigation by the State government? The entire petroleum business is non-transparent. Consumers do not have a mechanism of knowing the exact quantity and quality. During our inspection, we found, to our dismay, that 85 per cent of the [fuel] guns were not dispensing the correct quantity. Then we also ventured into checking the quality. The system is such that oil companies supply fuel and also certify their own quality. In order to determine the quantity of ethanol in the fuel, we collected 63 samples across the State through an understanding with oil marketing companies [OMCs] and petroleum dealers and gave those samples to the OMCs. They did not give a clear answer on the percentage of ethanol blended for any one of the 63 samples. That made us suspicious. What options were left with us? We had to collect more samples as per the law, which were jointly collected by all three parties, duly signed in the proforma. The testing was conducted by an NABL-accredited third-party lab. The result was that ethanol was being blended up to 31.2 per cent. Were the OMC representatives present on both occasions? Yes, and they have signed the proforma. The oil companies and the BJP claim that the tests you conducted are limited to the “gas chromatography” procedure, without going into details. Additionally, the OMCs have asked how the density for E26-E31 fuel was less than that for E20, which they measured, since ethanol is more dense than petrol. They can technically say anything. The lab has used gas chromatography. They say that this is the right method. I went to the OMCs first, gave them 63 samples, and requested a test result. In response, they were ambiguous, vague, and tried to dodge us. We selected the samples and their representative signed on the proforma. They also have a set of the samples. If the density recorded in the proforma was different from the one seen in the result, one could doubt the labs. But that hasn’t changed. A few months ago, there was a big controversy over E20 itself. What is the Karnataka government’s official position on E20? We are not against blending ethanol with petrol. However, engines should be able to digest ethanol-inclusive petrol. Petrol pumps must possess the required infrastructure to dispense such fuel. Brazil, for example, is blending up to 30 per cent ethanol (E30). But they took 50 years (beginning in 1975) to reach that stage by producing ethanol-complaint vehicles and created the infrastructure. Here, the Modi government is pushing the fuel without building the necessary infrastructure. E20-compliant vehicles are being produced in the country from 2023 onwards. Out of the 35 crore vehicles in India, how many are E20-compliant? Very few. Then why are they only pushing E20 fuel for [older] vehicles? What happens to the engines of vehicles made for pure petrol [those manufactured before 2008]? The performance of the engine will reduce and repair costs will soar. The Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers, which produces E20-compliant vehicles, has written to the Central government that sulphur and chloride content in the ethanol-blended fuel is high, and that vehicles are facing issues. That means they are either unofficially exceeding the 20 per cent ethanol limit, or those engines are not able to deal with E20 fuel. Since this transition takes time, we feel the government should first work on the infrastructure and then on the fuel. Secondly, until everything is ready, give a choice for the consumer to choose between pure, E10, E20, and beyond E20 petrol. You have termed it a conflict of interest for oil companies to both test and sell oil. Do you also consider Union Minister Nitin Gadkari promoting ethanol-blended fuel as a conflict of interest as his sons run agro-industrial and distillery businesses? Of course. Nitin Gadkariji was promoting ethanol and speaks more about ethanol than the Petroleum Minister himself. Let him propagate ethanol and its advantages. However, your own children are running ethanol-producing factories, and you, as a Union Minister, are promoting it. There is some sort of a conflict of interest here. Secondly, the Central government’s faulty policies have resulted in many influential persons owning ethanol-producing factories. They produce a lot of ethanol, but the infrastructure is not yet ready for ethanol blending. It is also quite expensive. The Centre has pushed ethanol-producing factories so much that our ethanol, I am told, is more expensive than it is on the international market. If you don’t blend it, where will it go? The Central government should prioritise the common people’s interest instead of the lobbies’. You have made strong claims and stood by them. What next? Very soon, I shall write to the Central government, hoping that they take note of this. We are seeking a system where OMCs can test their fuel for quality checking but not for compliance, which concerns the consumers. There has to be a third-party independent testing mechanism established in every State where the fuel quality is tested randomly, time and again, and reports are shared. Secondly, we request the Central government to work on the infrastructure needed for ethanol blending. By a conservative estimate of a 10 per cent drop in mileage for a vehicle, consumers will lose over Rs.60,000 crore per year. A monthly repair cost of around Rs.2,000-3,000 will cause a loss of over Rs.40,000 crore for users (cumulatively). The deadline for E20 was 2030, but the Central government has reduced it by five years. This is causing problems for the public. How confident are you of a favourable reply from the Central government? If the Central government acts in the interest of the people, they will give a favourable reply. If not, how will you proceed? Then we will go all out, keep testing and bringing out things. As a State government elected by the people, we are responsible for protecting their rights. Once I revealed this, they should have sought full information with an intention to rectify if things are wrong. What’s my personal interest in this? I am a youngster who recently became a Minister and am enthusiastic to work. I am aware that I am fighting a mighty government having IT, ED, CBI, NIA, etc. The vindictive reputation of this government regarding its political rivals is well known. If this was not genuine, why would I take such a risk? Once you came out with this, Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi picked this up, while the Congress government in Keralam is also proceeding along similar lines. However, is there a national-level consensus within the INDIA bloc on this? I am happy that Rahul Gandhiji has taken it up. That means he has endorsed an issue where people are suffering. I am sure he will fearlessly raise this issue in Parliament and hold the government accountable. Regarding the issue of some petrol-dispensing guns not delivering the required quantity of fuel, you had urged the Central government to reduce the error tolerance levels from 0.5 per cent to 0.3 per cent, as in some Western countries. What was the response? I am pained to say that the Central government hasn’t replied to any of my suggestions. We had also told the Central government that we cannot follow their guidelines of calibrating fuel-dispensing guns once in two years, as against the earlier one-year rule. They have also noted that the calibration can also be done by government-approved test centres. If any such centre does it, there will be a conflict of interest. A lot of things can happen between dealers and government-approved test centres. We mentioned that too, to the Central government, but they have not replied. Ethanol blending: Who gains and who pays? Ethanol blending: Who gains and who pays? The new E20 policy transfers costs onto consumers by way of lower mileage and higher maintenance, while offering limited gains to farmers and strong incentives to ethanol distillers. headline: Odisha Government Announces 15 Major Decisions to Strengthen Education System and Ensure Welfare of Teachers and Employees | Chief Minister of Odisha
content: The State Government is always committed to strengthening the state's education system and ensuring the welfare of teachers, lecturers and employees. Considering the recommendations of the Ashok Tripathy Committee, constituted to examine the demands raised by various teachers' and employees' associations, Chief Minister Shri Mohan Charan Majhi, at a high-level meeting today, decided to implement the following 15 important recommendations: ✅ Bringing 194 high schools under the grant-in-aid system that were deprived of benefits under the 2013 Government Block Grant scheme. ✅ Increasing the monthly remuneration of part-time Art, Music and Sports Teachers working in government schools from Rs. 10,000 to Rs. 16,000. ✅ Payment of arrears of salary to TGT and PET teachers of government secondary schools who completed six years of service and were regularised in 2022. ✅ Regularisation of Sikhya Sahayaks appointed between 2016 and 2018.

headline: Chhattisgarh CM announces ₹13,839 per acre aid for paddy farmers irrespective of yield
content: Final URL: https://government.economictimes.indiatimes.com/news/governance/chhattisgarh-cm-announces-13839-per-acre-aid-for-paddy-farmers-irrespective-of-yield/135776518 The decision will benefit farmers in tribal-dominated Bastar and Surguja divisions, where paddy yield is relatively lower than in other parts of the state, Chhattisgarh Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai added. The BJP government in Chhattisgarh has decided to provide paddy farmers input assistance of ₹13,839 per acre under its Krishak Unnati Yojana, irrespective of the quantity they sell, Chief Minister Vishnu Deo Sai said on Thursday. The decision will benefit farmers in tribal-dominated Bastar and Surguja divisions, where paddy yield is relatively lower than in other parts of the state, Sai added. Addressing a press conference at the BJP's state headquarters here, Sai said the government currently procures up to 21 quintals of paddy per acre from farmers in the Kharif marketing season, but cultivators in Bastar and Surguja often fail to produce that much due to lower yields.

headline: Building Women Entrepreneurs Through the Dakshayani Self-Entrepreneurship Assistance Scheme
content: The Scheduled Caste, Scheduled Tribe and Backward Classes Development Department has launched the Dakshayani Self-Help Groups Scheme to promote economic empowerment and entrepreneurship among Scheduled Caste women in Kerala. The scheme has been introduced to provide a long-term solution to the financial challenges faced by women from Scheduled Caste communities and to help them achieve economic independence through self-employment and entrepreneurship. Named after Dakshayani Velayudhan, the only Dalit woman who served in the Constituent Assembly of India, the scheme was launched on her birth anniversary. The pilot project has been introduced in Palakkad district and will be expanded to other districts after its successful implementation. Under the scheme, self-help groups of Scheduled Caste women can receive substantial financial assistance to start new enterprises or expand existing businesses. The scheme is open to registered groups whose members are above 18 years of age and are registered with government departments or recognised agencies. For new enterprises, the government will provide a subsidy of up to 75% of the total project cost, subject to a maximum of ₹10 lakh. The remaining 25% can be raised through bank loans or financial assistance from the SC/ST Development Corporation. Groups that have been successfully running enterprises for at least two years can also receive financial support to expand their businesses. A subsidy of up to ₹5 lakh is available for enterprise expansion. Priority under the scheme will be given to women from Below Poverty Line (BPL) families, members of vulnerable groups, single mothers, widows, transgender persons, those registered with the Kerala Startup Mission or NORKA, and unemployed women who have completed professional courses. The scheme is expected to help women from Scheduled Caste communities overcome financial hardships, become self-reliant, and build sustainable livelihoods through entrepreneurship. By encouraging women to move beyond traditional occupations and seize new business opportunities, the Dakshayani Self-Help Groups Scheme aims to create lasting economic and social empowerment while honouring the legacy of social reformer Dakshayani Velayudhan.

headline: FIR registered against Kangana Ranaut in Himachal Pradesh over social media posts on Gandhi family
content: Shimla: Himachal Pradesh Police on Friday registered an FIR against BJP MP Kangana Ranaut following a complaint over her social media posts on the Gandhi family that included "highly inflammatory insinuations" regarding the deaths of former prime minister Indira Gandhi and her sons Sanjay and Rajiv. .Superintendent of Police (Shimla) Gaurav Singh said the case has been registered on the complaint by Shimla resident Capt. Atul Sharma and investigations will follow. .The case was registered under sections 196, 353 and 356 of BNS. .Sharma alleged that Ranaut's posts through her verified handle on November 10 contained highly inflammatory insinuations regarding the tragic deaths of Indira Gandhi, Sanjay Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi. .'Mysterious foreigner': Kangana Ranaut attacks Sonia Gandhi, says Maneka was 'thrown out' of house.In his complaint to the Director General of Police sent via mail (a copy of which is available with the PTI), he demanded the immediate registration of an FIR and a rigorous, time-bound cyber-forensic investigation against Ranaut. .The complaint was sent at 7:51 pm on Thursday night. .According to Sharma, the posts also describe Congress leader Sonia Gandhi as a "mysterious foreign national" who allegedly landed in a cafe abroad before relatives were killed one after another, leaving her as the head of government with the chilling remark: "How convenient". .It also alleged the abrupt expulsion of Maneka Gandhi from the family residence following Sanjay Gandhi's death. .Sharma asserted that this calculated narrative crosses the line from political dissent into dangerous territory capable of inciting public hostility and disturbing public tranquillity. .The complainant alleged that the posts constituted public mischief by circulating false information with the intent to cause fear or alarm. .They could promote enmity between different groups and act prejudicial to the maintenance of harmony, and contain imputations and assertions prejudicial to national integration.

headline: Himachal Government Moves to Take Over Land Bought Using Fake Agriculturist Certificates in Kangra
content: Dharamshala: The Himachal Pradesh government is preparing to initiate action against individuals who allegedly purchased land in Kangra district using fraudulent agriculturist certificates, with the possibility of transferring such illegally acquired land into the name of the state government. The investigation has gathered momentum, particularly around Gaggal Airport, where multiple cases of alleged violations and manipulation of revenue records have come to light. According to information emerging from the investigation, six cases involving the sale and purchase of more than 200 kanals of land, collectively valued at several crores of rupees, have surfaced between January and October this year. The cases have brought alleged misuse of agriculturist certificates and manipulation of revenue records under the scanner, prompting the Vigilance Bureau to widen its investigation. The Vigilance Bureau is now preparing to send a detailed communication to the Kangra district administration, placing all relevant facts and findings before the Deputy Commissioner. The district administration will subsequently examine the cases and initiate appropriate legal proceedings, including action for transferring the land to the state government wherever violations are established under the applicable law. The investigation initially gained momentum in January, when the Vigilance Bureau registered FIRs against several individuals. They were accused of manipulating revenue records in Palampur and Dharamshala to facilitate land transactions. During the investigation, officials reportedly uncovered additional instances of land purchases near Gaggal Airport allegedly carried out using fake agriculturist certificates. This led to the registration of further cases involving different families and individuals. In July, the Vigilance Bureau registered a case against a couple from Dunga Bazar in Kangra and their relatives. Subsequently, in August, two more cases were registered against a family from Gaggal and others over alleged illegal financial transactions conducted through a firm.

headline: A Railway Above the Clouds: Bilaspur-Manali-Leh Line Could Put India on Top of the World
content: Imagine stepping out of a train at a railway station perched nearly 17,600 feet above sea level, surrounded by towering Himalayan peaks, snow-covered mountain passes and some of the world’s most challenging terrain. At this altitude, even breathing becomes an effort, temperatures can plunge dramatically, and the landscape appears almost otherworldly. This could one day become a reality in India. The proposed Bilaspur-Manali-Leh railway line, one of the most ambitious railway infrastructure projects envisioned in the Himalayas, could feature the world’s highest railway station at Tengla in Ladakh, near the Tanglang La mountain pass. At an estimated altitude of 17,582 feet (5,359 metres), the proposed Tengla station could surpass China’s Tanggula railway station in Tibet, which stands at approximately 16,627 feet (5,068 metres) and is widely recognised as the world’s highest railway station. If realised as proposed, the Indian station would rewrite the record books and place the country at the forefront of high-altitude railway engineering. But the significance of this railway line goes far beyond a world record. It represents an extraordinary engineering ambition: taking the railway network through some of the most inaccessible, geographically challenging and strategically sensitive regions of the Indian Himalayas. The proposed railway corridor will stretch approximately 489 kilometres, connecting Beri/Bilaspur in Himachal Pradesh with Leh in Ladakh. It will pass through some of the most spectacular yet geographically challenging terrain of the Himalayas. The proposed alignment includes Sundernagar, Mandi, Manali, Sissu, Darcha, Keylong, Sarchu, Pang, Rumtse, Upshi and Kharu before terminating at Leh. For residents of these remote mountain settlements, the railway could transform access to education, healthcare, markets and employment opportunities.

headline: FIR against BJP MP Kangana over posts on Gandhi family
content: Shimla: Shimla Police have registered an FIR against BJP MP from Mandi Kangana Ranaut over her alleged objectionable social media posts concerning the Gandhi family, SSP Gaurav Singh said on Friday.The FIR was registered following a complaint filed by Shimla resident Capt Atul Sharma (retd), who had approached Himachal Pradesh DGP Ashok Tewari seeking action against the actor-turned-politician over a post published on her verified social media account on Nov 10.In his complaint, Sharma objected to the post, which allegedly juxtaposed the deaths of former prime ministers Indira Gandhi and Rajiv Gandhi, and Congress leader Sanjay Gandhi, with Sonia Gandhi’s subsequent political rise, using expressions such as “how convenient”. He also objected to the post allegedly portraying Sonia Gandhi as a mysterious foreign national.The complainant alleged that the post could create misleading impressions of suspicious connections between the deaths and political succession. He urged police to examine the matter under Sections 196 and 353 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), citing concerns over potentially inflammatory and unsubstantiated imputations.He also sought a cyber forensic examination to establish the post’s authenticity, context and dissemination, along with verification of the archival video referenced in it.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Chandigarh | Silver Rate in Chandigarh | Bank Holidays in Chandigarh | Public Holidays in Chandigarh | Chandigarh AQI | Weather in Chandigarh | Petrol Price in Chandigarh | Diesel Price in Chandigarh | CNG Price in Chandigarh | LPG Price in ChandigarhStay updated with the latest Chandigarh news. headline: Himachal Congress Crisis: Kullu MLA Berth Delay Sparks Worker Outrage
content: SHIMLA: Discontent has emerged within the Himachal Pradesh Congress party, with a significant number of workers from Kullu expressing strong resentment over the prolonged delay in inducting local MLA Sunder Singh Thakur into the state Cabinet. Reports indicate that over 200 workers from block and mandal-level units in Kullu have threatened mass resignations if their demand for Thakur's inclusion is not met.According to details received by The Chenab Times, these workers voiced their displeasure during a meeting held at the circuit house in Kullu. Sunder Singh Thakur was reportedly present at this meeting, where discussions revolved around the protracted delay in the cabinet expansion and the possibility of submitting collective resignations.The Chief Minister, Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu, had previously indicated that Thakur would be inducted into the Cabinet. However, a recent remark by the Chief Minister, suggesting that Thakur would become a minister when his 'stars favoured him,' has reportedly caused significant upset among a section of party workers. This statement has also drawn criticism from the opposition, with Leader of the Opposition and former Chief Minister Jai Ram Thakur sarcastically urging Sunder Singh Thakur at a rally not to accept a Cabinet berth if it compromised his dignity.Sunder Singh Thakur was among the six MLAs who were appointed as chief parliamentary secretaries (CPS) prior to the cabinet expansion on January 8, 2023. However, these appointments were later quashed by the high court. Following this, Thakur emerged as a frontrunner for the single vacant ministerial berth in the state Cabinet.Adding to the growing unrest, a poster featuring Sunder Singh Thakur has gained traction on social media platforms. The poster carries the message, "For self-respect and for the development of Kullu, I can do anything." The Sukhu-led government is nearing the completion of its four-year term on December 11, 2026, with the next Assembly elections anticipated in November 2027.The issue has underscored deeper concerns within the party regarding the representation of districts in the state Cabinet. Sunder Singh Thakur himself has emphasized that the matter is not about personal ambition but about the dignity and self-respect of Kullu and its people. He noted that the district has historically been represented in the state Cabinet since the tenure of Himachal Pradesh's first Chief Minister, Yashwant Singh Parmar, and that Kullu's identity warrants government representation.Reports suggest that the delay in the cabinet expansion has become a source of embarrassment for the state leadership. While Thakur has dismissed speculation about leaving the Congress, he has acknowledged the sentiment among his supporters and indicated that party workers would decide the future course of action. The situation highlights a broader challenge for the Congress leadership in Himachal Pradesh, which is navigating internal factionalism and striving to maintain cohesion ahead of the upcoming elections. The party faces the intricate task of balancing regional representation, seniority, and political interests within its ranks.The discontent within the Congress in Kullu is indicative of a larger trend of dissatisfaction among grassroots workers who feel overlooked. This sentiment has been echoed by other party leaders who have raised concerns about appointments and the party's internal dynamics. The delay in filling the lone vacant ministerial berth, coupled with the internal dissent, could pose a challenge to the ruling party's stability and electoral prospects in the state.

headline: How safe are online dating platforms?
content: A recent post on X has once again highlighted the hazards of using dating apps. A user revealed that he received similar messages from two different matches on a popular dating app. They followed a ‘script’, asked him to meet them on Church Street and left the exact venue undecided. “First, they suggest meeting on Church Street. Then comes the classic line, ‘Let’s meet there and decide where to go’,” he posted. What eventually happens is the scamster takes the unsuspecting victim to a fancy cafe and runs up a huge bill, leaving the victim to foot it..While this scam has been running for years, it is only one among numerous safety issues faced by app users. Users Metrolife spoke to reported getting scammed and sexually assaulted..Studies say.According to a 2025 study from the Post Graduate Institute of Medical Education and Research, Chandigarh, dating app usage had a significant connection with higher STI prevalence (including HIV coinfection)..Literature reviews published in the Humanities and Social Sciences Communications journal document widespread technology-facilitated violence against women on Indian dating platforms, such as image-based abuse, cyberstalking, doxing, gender trolling, and unsolicited explicit media..Dating app trap: Four arrested in Bengaluru for assaulting, robbing man of Rs 37,000.Party scam.“The first time I got scammed, I was 18,” says 26-year-old Aman. While using an app for gay and bisexual men, he swiped right on a profile of “a really handsome guy”. “He said he was hosting a house party, and I accepted the invitation. I sneaked out of my house around midnight and went to the location he’d shared. It was an apartment building, and I was waiting in the basement when he messaged me. He said I had to pay an entry fee. I ended up paying Rs 1,000,” he recalls. It then took a turn for the worse. After the payment went through, he called the man to come pick him up from the basement. “The number had blocked me, his profile disappeared, and I was stranded in an unfamiliar parking lot. I eventually took an auto back home,” he shares..In another incident, Aman hit it off with a man who claimed he was 32. He later found out that the man was over 45. “I was creeped out at first, but eventually I came to terms with it,” says Aman, who was 20 at the time..Samanta K (name changed), a 22-year-old media professional, had a harrowing experience earlier this year. “It was our first date. We were at a popular bar on Church Street. The guy tried to kiss me, and I dodged it. He apologised immediately and claimed he misread the moment. However, he kept trying to invade my personal space,” she shares. When she stepped out to smoke, he followed her and behaved inappropriately. When she cut the date short and booked herself a cab, he forced his way into the cab and rode with her all the way to her house in R R Nagar. “In the cab, he continued to try his luck with me. It was very disturbing and took me months to heal,” she reveals..Increasingly common.According to advocate Indra Dhanush, these cases are becoming increasingly common, especially since the pandemic years. He takes on three to four such cases per month. “Most of them are booked under rape, Section 63, of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita. One of my clients claims she was taken advantage of when under the influence of alcohol and not in a position to give her consent,” he shares, adding that a majority of the victims are Gen Z..Additional regulations?.Researcher and tech policy expert Pranesh Prakash believes that additional regulation is not the solution. If the apps gather more information from users, it’s a violation of privacy and makes sensitive information vulnerable to data breaches, he explains, citing the example of a cybersecurity threat faced by Match Group (the parent company of Tinder and Hinge, among others) in January this year. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act was passed in 2023, but is only partially in force. Once it is fully rolled out, it could solve some problems, he points out.

headline: After Peterhoff, BJP Raises Questions Over Private Operation of Himachal Niketan
content: Shimla: The BJP has accused the Congress-led Himachal Pradesh government of moving towards handing over the management of another public property to private operators, raising questions over the proposed operation of the newly constructed Himachal Niketan in Dwarka, New Delhi. BJP chief spokesperson and Sundernagar MLA Rakesh Jamwal alleged that the government was increasingly looking towards commercialising public assets instead of prioritising facilities for the people of the state. Jamwal said the 107-room Himachal Niketan was constructed to provide accommodation to people from Himachal Pradesh visiting the national capital, particularly patients, their attendants, students and other visitors. At the time of its inauguration, Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu had projected the facility as an important initiative for the welfare of Himachalis. However, the government has now issued a tender for the selection of a private agency to operate, maintain and manage the property, he said. Questioning the government’s decision, Jamwal remarked, “Himachal Niketan is not the private property of the Congress Party. It belongs to the people of Himachal Pradesh. The move to hand over the management of a facility built for public welfare to private hands exposes the glaring contradiction between your government’s promises and its actions.” Referring to media reports suggesting that approximately 70 per cent of Himachal Niketan could be managed by a private agency, the BJP leader expressed concern over the availability of rooms and concessional accommodation for ordinary Himachalis. He alleged that the proposed arrangement could create difficulties for economically weaker patients and their families who travel to Delhi for medical treatment and depend on affordable government accommodation. He also questioned whether adequate facilities would remain available for students and other residents of Himachal Pradesh visiting the national capital.

headline: “Will quit Congress if not made minister by December 11”: BJP's Baldev Tomar targets Sukhu government over Sunder Singh Thakur's ultimatum
content: Shimla (Himachal Pradesh) [India], November 13 (ANI): Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) spokesperson Baldev Tomar on Friday alleged that internal differences within the ruling Congress in Himachal Pradesh were surfacing publicly, citing Kullu MLA Sunder Singh Thakur's reported ultimatum over his induction into the state Cabinet.Referring to a report published in the media, Tomar said Thakur had indicated that he could part ways with the Congress if he was not given a ministerial position by December 11. He described the development as a significant political challenge for Chief Minister Sukhvinder Singh Sukhu."The ultimatum from the Kullu MLA is now before the Chief Minister. Whether he is made a minister by December 11 or not, everyone within and outside the Congress will be watching," Tomar said."He further said that, according to the newspaper report, Thakur had conveyed his displeasure to party functionaries, raising concerns about his self-respect and the honour of the people of Kullu."Tomar said, "The issue had gone beyond the demand for a ministerial berth, as the MLA had also linked it to the political representation and dignity of his constituency. The BJP leader further claimed that although Chief Minister Sukhu had earlier indicated that Thakur could be inducted into the Cabinet, the legislator's decision to set a deadline had raised questions about the government's decision-making process.""The timing of the public disagreement said that people in Himachal Pradesh expected the government to address issues such as unemployment, development works and economic challenges. The Congress leadership should clarify the reasons behind the delay in Cabinet expansion and its response to the concerns raised by the Kullu MLA," Tomar said.He added that Thakur's statement was an example of growing resentment within the Congress, and all eyes would now be on the decision taken by the Chief Minister and the party leadership before December 11. (ANI)

headline: J P Nadda reviews development and healthcare services at Rural Health Training Centre in Najafgarh
content: 13/11/26 | 9:45 pm | J P Nadda reviews development and healthcare services | Rural Health Training Centre in Najafgarh | Union Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda Union Health and Family Welfare Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda on Friday reviewed the institutional progress and development of the Rural Health Training Centre (RHTC) in Najafgarh, Delhi, under the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. During the review, the minister was briefed on the institution’s progress in hospital and patient care services, diagnostic facilities, human resources, academic infrastructure, quality assurance and community-based healthcare delivery. Addressing officials and healthcare personnel, Nadda appreciated the efforts made by RHTC Najafgarh to strengthen its infrastructure and healthcare services. He said the institution was progressing in the right direction and commended its team for implementing various development initiatives. He also acknowledged the contributions of Safdarjung Hospital and the Health Ministry in supporting the centre’s growth, expressing confidence that continued cooperation among stakeholders would help develop RHTC into an important centre for patient care, medical education and community healthcare. RHTC Najafgarh recorded significant patient footfall between August and October 2026, attending to 94,927 patients in its Outpatient Department (OPD) across 10 specialities and providing emergency services to 35,985 patients. The hospital also recorded 198 inpatient admissions during the period.

headline: Car at 200 kmph smashes into Dwarka tunnel wall, engine ripped out, driver killed
content: A 22-year-old man was killed after his car, moving at around 200 kmph, crashed into a wall inside the Dwarka Expressway airport tunnel, ripping the engine out of the vehicle and triggering a fire, police said on Thursday, PTI reported.The victim, Abhinav Singh, was on his way from Ludhiana to Gurugram when the accident occurred near the Shiv Murti interchange. Police suspect the car was speeding at around 200 kmph, well above the speed limit of 80 kmph.Singh, a native of Muzaffarpur in Bihar, lived in Sector 42, Gurugram. Police said he was driving a modified Volkswagen Virtus belonging to a friend. He had gone to Ludhiana to meet his girlfriend and was returning to Gurugram on Diwali morning.According to PTI, the initial investigation found that Singh had allegedly recorded videos and photographs of the car's speedometer and sent them to his friends through Snapchat shortly before the crash. Police are trying to retrieve the material as part of the investigation.Police officials told PTI that CCTV footage from the tunnel showed the car travelling at very high speed before crashing near a turn connecting the tunnel to National Highway 48.The impact ripped the car's engine off and threw it some distance away, where it caught fire. Singh was trapped inside the mangled vehicle and died at the scene.Police have recorded the statements of security personnel deployed at the tunnel, as well as other motorists and eyewitnesses who were present at the spot. The Delhi Police is investigating the accident.Singh's body was sent for a post-mortem examination and later handed over to his family, officials told PTI. His mother is a teacher and lives in Bihar.The Dwarka Expressway airport tunnel has a maximum speed limit of 80 kmph. Two-wheelers, auto-rickshaws, tractors, non-motorised vehicles and tankers carrying inflammable substances are prohibited inside it.Police are examining CCTV footage, witness statements and Singh's alleged social media posts to investigate the crash, in which the 22-year-old died after his car hit a tunnel wall at high speed.- Ends

headline: Pollution can harm your heart even without a cough: How toxic air damages blood vessels and silently rais
content: Air pollution is discussed in the context of coughing, breathing difficulties and damaged lungs. But there is another organ that quietly bears the burden of toxic air: the heart. Even when pollution does not cause an immediate cough or breathing problem, tiny particles in the air can enter the bloodstream and affect the cardiovascular system. Over time, this exposure can damage blood vessels, raise blood pressure and increase the risk of heart attacks and strokes.The concern is particularly serious in cities where poor air quality lasts for weeks. The heart does not get a break simply because a person stays indoors or does not have an existing respiratory condition.How polluted air reaches the heartFine particulate matter, especially PM2.5, is small enough to travel deep into the lungs. Some particles and the biological responses they trigger can affect the circulatory system. This can cause inflammation and damage the lining of blood vessels.Dr P. K. Rustagi, Senior Consultant – Interventional Cardiologist at Jaipur Golden Hospital, Rohini, Delhi, explained, "Air pollution is not just a respiratory health concern; it is also a major risk factor for cardiovascular diseases. Fine particulate matter (PM2.5) can trigger inflammation, damage blood vessels and increase the risk of heart-related complications."Why pollution can trigger a heart attackPollution can affect several processes that keep the heart functioning normally. It may increase blood pressure, promote inflammation and interfere with blood clotting. In someone with narrowed coronary arteries, these changes can make an already vulnerable heart more likely to experience an acute event.Dr Rustagi explained, "Exposure to high levels of air pollution can increase the risk of heart attacks. Pollutants can cause inflammation, elevate blood pressure and affect blood clotting mechanisms, potentially triggering acute cardiac events."Long-term exposure can damage arteriesThe danger is not limited to a few heavily polluted days. Repeated exposure over months and years can accelerate atherosclerosis, a condition in which fatty deposits build up inside arteries. These deposits narrow the blood vessels and can restrict blood flow.This raises the risk of heart attacks, strokes and other cardiovascular complications. It also means that pollution-related heart damage may develop quietly, without obvious warning signs.Who needs to be more careful?Pollution can affect anyone, but the consequences may be more serious for people whose hearts are already under strain. Those with coronary artery disease, hypertension or heart failure face a greater risk of complications.Senior citizens and people with diabetes also need to be cautious. They should not assume that staying indoors during peak pollution hours is enough to eliminate exposure.The scale of the problem is reflected in India's own health data. A Ministry of Health and Family Welfare advisory, citing an ICMR study, reported that air pollution contributed to 1.7 million deaths in India in 2019. Ischaemic heart disease accounted for 29.2% of these pollution-attributable deaths. Read the government advisory.Steps to protect the heart during pollution spikesDr Rustagi recommended avoiding strenuous outdoor activities during severe pollution episodes. Wearing a well-fitted N95 mask outdoors, maintaining better indoor air quality and continuing prescribed medicines are also important precautions.People with existing heart conditions should avoid stopping medication or changing doses without medical advice. Exercise remains important for heart health, but outdoor workouts may need to be shifted indoors when air quality deteriorates.Chest pain, unusual breathlessness or sudden discomfort should never be dismissed as a routine effect of pollution. These symptoms need immediate medical attention.The US Environmental Protection Agency's scientific assessment of particulate matter also highlights evidence linking both short-term and long-term PM2.5 exposure with cardiovascular complications, including heart attacks, strokes and changes in blood pressure.Ultimately, protecting the heart during pollution season requires more than avoiding a morning walk. It means recognising that the air people breathe every day can influence their cardiovascular health long before symptoms appear.

headline: Delhi’s air quality turns hazardous as AQI touches 494
content: Delhi’s air quality deteriorated to hazardous levels on Friday morning, with the overall Air Quality Index (AQI) touching 494 at 7.31 am. Dense fog and pollution enveloped the national capital, reducing visibility across several areas, while multiple monitoring stations recorded severe pollution levels.According to Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data, IIT Delhi recorded an AQI of 488, followed by ITO at 455, Anand Vihar at 419, Rohini at 413 and Rajokri Border at 402, all falling in the severe category.Other areas also reported very poor air quality, with R K Puram recording an AQI of 391, Mandir Marg 378, Dwarka Expressway 369, Uttam Nagar 363 and Lodhi Road 341. The area around Dhaula Kuan recorded an AQI of 161, placing it in the moderate category.The Delhi government has been undertaking pollution-control measures, including deploying water sprinklers across the city, to minimise the impact of particulate matter.Meanwhile, AAP leader Saurabh Bharadwaj on Thursday accused the BJP government of misrepresenting Delhi’s pollution levels and questioned the credibility of the CPCB’s AQI readings. Citing a report by the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air (CREA), he alleged that actual pollution levels were 49 per cent higher than those displayed on official government websites..Speaking to ANI, Bharadwaj claimed that an AQI reading of 370 could have corresponded to an actual level of 560 or higher.“CREA showed that the pollution shown for Delhi was 49% higher than what you were told—meaning it was almost one and a half times higher,” he said.Bharadwaj also questioned the CPCB’s explanation on the limits of its monitoring system, alleging that readings exceeding 999 were not displayed.“The CPCB said that when our pollution level hits 999, we don't even consider that level, because we can't measure above 999 and we don't display 999. So it's just shown as zero,” he told ANI.He alleged that the discrepancy amounted to a fraud against Delhi’s two crore residents, saying it put the health of children and elderly people at risk.The allegations followed a CREA analysis of hourly PM2.5 data from 59 monitoring stations in Delhi. The report identified 255 missing hourly station records between 4 pm on November 8 and 4 pm on November 9. It also recorded a rise in the 24-hour average PM2.5 concentration from 269 to 400 micrograms per cubic metre, an increase of nearly 49 per cent.(With inputs from ANI).Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest

headline: Himachal Clears Path for Medicinal Cannabis Production, Licences Issued to Three Pharma Companies
content: Shimla: Himachal Pradesh has taken a significant step towards developing a regulated medicinal cannabis industry, with the state government issuing licences to three pharmaceutical companies and around 24 farmers for controlled cannabis cultivation. The initiative is expected to pave the way for the production of cannabis-based medicines in the state, with commercial activities likely to begin this year. Following the government’s decision to permit controlled cannabis cultivation for medicinal and industrial purposes, licences have been issued to two pharmaceutical companies in Baddi and one in Paonta Sahib. In addition, around 24 farmers from Kullu, Mandi and Shimla districts have obtained licences to cultivate cannabis under the state’s notified policy. The government is now making arrangements to supply certified seeds to the licensed farmers to ensure that cultivation takes place under regulated conditions and meets the prescribed quality standards. The initiative is being viewed as an opportunity to diversify Himachal Pradesh’s agricultural economy, increase farmers’ income and attract fresh investment in the state’s pharmaceutical sector. It is also expected to create employment opportunities in cultivation, processing, research and medicine manufacturing. To encourage farmers and pharmaceutical companies to participate in the initiative, the state government has substantially reduced the annual licence fees under the Second Amendment Rules, 2026, notified by the State Taxes and Excise Department. Under the revised provisions, the annual licence fee for farmers has been reduced from ₹3 lakh to ₹1 lakh per bigha. Similarly, the annual licence fee for processing and manufacturing units has been brought down from ₹2 crore to ₹1 crore.

headline: Ministry of Culture Convenes "Creative India: Collective Possibilities" at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi; Invites Partners to Build India's Creative Economy Together
content: The Ministry of Culture, Government of India, today organised "Creative India: Collective Possibilities", a conference on collaborative models for India's creative economy, at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. Inaugurated by Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat, Hon'ble Union Minister for Culture, the Conclave brought together representatives of the Central and State Governments, the Ministry's institutions, industry, philanthropy, the creative community and international partners, to explore how India's cultural wealth can contribute more fully to growth, livelihoods and India's place in the world. "The creative power of India is its real power," said Shri Gajendra Singh Shekhawat. "Ours is a living civilisation, whose creativity belongs to every region and every generation. As the world turns to an economy of ideas and imagination, our task is to connect this talent with opportunity, so that India's culture becomes a foundation of its prosperity and of its voice in the world." "Government's role is to be a catalyst," said Shri Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary, Ministry of Culture. "When the Ministry opens the door and partners carry the work forward, our heritage becomes a living resource for communities, artists and enterprise alike. The Creative Economy Division has been created to build exactly these partnerships." Setting the context, Shri Inderjeet Singh, IAS, Joint Secretary (Creative Economy), placed culture at the heart of India's development agenda, from the Kashi Culture Pathway to the vision of Viksit Bharat. He described the Ministry's 43 organisations, from more than 3,600 protected monuments to museums, archives, Akademis and Zonal Cultural Centres, as the public infrastructure of India's creative economy. As custodian of India's heritage, collections and living traditions, he said, the Ministry offers a natural meeting point for the many sectors, enterprises and creators that draw on India's culture. Partnerships are already in motion. The National Culture Fund has completed 66 projects with 39 partners since 1996, and Adopt a Heritage engages partners at 66 monuments. The sacred Piprahwa relics returned home through a partnership with Godrej Industries Group, Sabhyata Foundation has brought cultural evenings to Purana Qila, and the India Pavilion at Venice 2026 was realised with the Nita Mukesh Ambani Cultural Centre and Serendipity Arts Foundation. A new MoU with Google Arts & Culture will carry India's heritage to audiences worldwide. Four sessions, on Investing in Culture, Culture-Led Spaces, Culturepreneurs, and Technology and Communication, brought patrons, investors, heritage practitioners, designers, entrepreneurs and technology leaders into conversation. The deliberations explored trusted routes for philanthropy and private capital, monuments, museums and festivals as living destinations, pathways from livelihood to enterprise for artisans and designers, and new ways of carrying India's knowledge and narratives to the world on India's own terms.
